newsitem.title: USA: Former Ohio politician Vernal Riffe dies.
newsitem.headline: Former Ohio politician Vernal Riffe dies.

text.p: Vernal Riffe Jr., a powerful figure in Ohio politics for decades and the nation's senior leader of a state legislature at the close of his career, died Thursday, a hospital spokesman said.
Riffe, 72, had been undergoing treatment for lymphoma cancer after being admitted to Ohio State University Medical Centre for a lump in his neck May 5.

Republican Sen. Mike DeWine described Riffe as a "pragmatic, results-oriented speaker" in his record 20 years as the most powerful member of the Ohio House of Representatives. Riffe retired in 1994, and the Almanac of American Politics said he was then the nation's longest-serving state House Speaker.

"He learned that in a legislative body, you get a lot further by helping your colleagues move their own legislation forward than you do by grandstanding," DeWine said in a statement to be delivered on the floor of the U.S. Senate.
Riffe's worked easily with Ohio's Republican governors, and former Gov. Richard Celeste referred to him as "the prime minister."
The Columbus Dispatch reported Riffe, a moderate Democrat, pushed through only three bills of his own in 36 years in the House. Often mentioned as a potential governor, Riffe never ran for the post.
Riffe, who once worked as an insurance salesman, learned at the feet of his father who was mayor of the southern Ohio town of New Boston for more than two decades.
He is survived by his wife Thelma, four children, and seven grandchildren.
